business.name: Houston Roofing & Construction
business.tagline: We inspect. We show you. You decide.

founded.note: Business site says 2009; Blue Book says 2008.

business.ownership: Locally owned and operated, family-owned per business profiles
business.workModel: In-house project managers; the business says it does not subcontract roof projects.

credentials.label: BBB A+ Rating
credentials.plainEnglish: The Better Business Bureau grades businesses A+ to F based on complaint history, transparency and other factors. A+ is the top grade.

credentials.label: GAF Master Elite (President's Club level)
credentials.plainEnglish: GAF is the largest shingle manufacturer in North America. Master Elite is its top contractor tier, and certified contractors can offer GAF's strongest manufacturer warranties. President's Club is described by the business as GAF's highest award.
credentials.notes: Business blog says 8 straight years as of its post; do not hard-code the year count.

credentials.label: RCAT Licensed
credentials.plainEnglish: Texas has no state license for roofers. The Roofing Contractors Association of Texas runs a voluntary licensing program, which the business holds.

credentials.label: FORTIFIED Roof
credentials.plainEnglish: FORTIFIED is a construction standard from the Insurance Institute for Business & Home Safety (IBHS) for roofs built to resist severe wind.

credentials.label: Owens Corning Preferred installer
credentials.plainEnglish: A contractor tier offered by Owens Corning for installers who meet its rigorous performance requirements.

credentials.label: Commercial manufacturer certifications (Carlisle, Duro-Last)
credentials.plainEnglish: Manufacturer certifications that allow commercial roof systems to carry certified manufacturer warranties.

hero.headline: A roof you can trust. A process you can see.
hero.subhead: Book a free inspection online, then follow every step of your project from your own dashboard.

process.title: Inspect
process.body: We look at the whole roof system: shingles, flashing, vents, penetrations and the trouble spots in between.

process.title: Show
process.body: You see what we see. Photos and plain-language notes land in your dashboard.

process.title: Explain
process.body: Repair or replace, and what each choice means for cost, lifespan and insurance. No pressure.

process.title: Install
process.body: A project manager from our own team oversees the job from first nail to final cleanup.

goodBetterBest.intro: Every project can include tiered options so you pick what fits your budget and how long you plan to own the property.

tiers.label: Good
tiers.title: Dependable asphalt shingles
tiers.body: A cost-conscious system built for Houston heat and storms.
tiers.bestFor: Budget-focused projects or shorter ownership plans

tiers.label: Better
tiers.title: Upgraded architectural system
tiers.body: Thicker, higher-performing shingles and a more complete component system.
tiers.bestFor: Most homeowners who want a balance of value and durability

tiers.label: Best
tiers.title: Long-life metal roofing
tiers.body: Metal panels designed for longevity and strong heat reflection.
tiers.bestFor: Owners planning to stay long term

warrantyExplainer.title: Warranties: read past the big number
points: A manufacturer warranty covers materials. Workmanship coverage is separate and just as important.
Warranties only help if the roof is installed to spec and the warranty is registered correctly.
Choose coverage that matches how long you realistically expect to own the property.
Ask whether the warranty transfers to a future buyer.
warrantyExplainer.note: The business describes a premium manufacturer warranty (it names GAF Golden Pledge). Confirm exact warranty names, terms and years before publishing.

compliance.insuranceDisclosure: We are roofing contractors, not public insurance adjusters. We do not negotiate or settle claims on your behalf. You are responsible for your insurance deductible. Texas law prohibits contractors from waiving, rebating or absorbing a deductible.
compliance.contractNotice: Contracts of $1,000 or more that involve an insurance settlement must include the statutory deductible notice (Tex. Bus. & Com. Code 27.02). TODO: have counsel supply the exact contract wording.
